examples.title: Winter lamp with wreath
examples.lesson: A dish shade, transparent round light and green life ring create a readable seasonal lamp with seven parts.
examples.placement_notes: The thin post has no pavement footing. Design its support before installation, and keep the wreath clear of pedestrians and nearby walls. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Ornamental globe lamp
examples.lesson: An inverted transparent globe and a sideways foliage sprig give a street fitting a distinctive silhouette.
examples.placement_notes: Reserve the round four-stud base and the asymmetric foliage envelope. Check the bar, globe and sprig interfaces when adapting its height. Connection analysis leaves 9 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Small ornamental tree
examples.lesson: Stacked brown cones and differently angled foliage produce a tapered trunk and a compact organic crown.
examples.placement_notes: Treat this as a narrow ornamental plant or a small tree at the chosen scene scale. Add a ground attachment; the source does not include a landscape base. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Layered woodland tree
examples.lesson: Round trunk courses and rotated foliage layers create a broad canopy with irregular edges.
examples.placement_notes: The green base is four studs square, but foliage spreads about 11.6 studs. Reserve that canopy envelope and adjust layer angles instead of simply scaling the source. Connection analysis leaves 5 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Moulded staircase and landing
examples.lesson: A dedicated staircase provides thin risers and an open underside with far fewer parts than stacked solid bricks.
examples.placement_notes: Reserve four studs across the stair and a twelve-stud source depth including the narrow upper landing. Match the actual landing height to the floor; add handrails where the brief needs them.

examples.title: Arched panel with side clips
examples.lesson: A small arch, grooved top edge and side clips combine a shaped opening with a useful attachment vocabulary.
examples.placement_notes: This is a narrow roof-notch wall insert, not a complete dormer. Preserve the side-clip clearance and source orientation, and inspect the adjoining roof before attaching a new panel.

examples.title: Two-track loading ramp
examples.lesson: Two wheel tracks, hinge fingers and a small grille communicate a functional loading surface while keeping the centre open.
examples.placement_notes: Measure the mating hinge in the host truck and match its finger spacing. Check both deployed and folded clearance; the source image shows only its stored local pose.

examples.title: Opening window with shutters
examples.lesson: Dedicated window leaves and louvred shutters add depth and a recognizable opening mechanism to a facade.
examples.placement_notes: Use the frame footprint for the wall opening, not the approximately 7.5-stud open-shutter envelope. Reserve front and side sweep and preserve the leaf pivots. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Timbered wall and projecting arches
examples.lesson: Patterned timber panels, a shutter and paired arches create strong architectural identity in a small wall section.
examples.placement_notes: The arches project well beyond the upright wall. Preserve their roof-support relationship, inspect the source base, and adapt the red palette deliberately to the new building.

examples.title: Airliner engine and pylon
examples.lesson: A dedicated cylindrical engine casing, turbine face and exhaust create a convincing nacelle with a thin brick-built pylon.
examples.placement_notes: Reserve the four-stud engine diameter and eleven-stud source length. Match the pylon top studs to the wing and check fan and exhaust clearances before repeating the module. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Sloped tail fin with beacon
examples.lesson: A sequence of slopes, a thin contrasting base and a transparent tip make a small fin recognizable from a distance.
examples.placement_notes: Use the six-stud long, narrow source profile as a scale reference. Side studs protrude beyond the nominal one-stud thickness; align the base to the fuselage and retain clearance.

examples.title: Tapered wing with hinge root
examples.lesson: Wedge plates establish a taper while hinge fingers, a grille and a small light give the wing a clear root and tip.
examples.placement_notes: The source is the left wing. Inspect the matching right assembly rather than assuming reflection preserves connectors; reserve the root hinge sweep and approximately 12.8-stud span.

examples.title: Classic compact truck tractor
examples.lesson: A moulded windscreen, doors, grille, lights and antenna make a compact truck read as a vehicle rather than a box.
examples.placement_notes: This source includes wheels and rear chassis as well as the cab. Inspect its coupling and wheel envelope before attaching a trailer; retain or replace the branded panel deliberately. Connection analysis leaves 8 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Mini construction truck cab
examples.lesson: A narrow windscreen, shaped roof, grille and small wheel assemblies convey construction-vehicle character at a compact scale.
examples.placement_notes: The cab body is only two studs wide with tyres extending beyond it. Use its actual dimensions instead of assuming minifigure seating, and build the rear body around the exposed chassis.

examples.title: Spacecraft wheel module
examples.lesson: Wheel-pin plates, a tall bracket and small exhaust and grille fittings give a compact wheeled module a mechanical identity.
examples.placement_notes: The original parent calls this landing gear; its isolated appearance also suggests rover ideas. Preserve the hinge and bracket interfaces and test deployed clearance in the parent before reuse. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Airliner wheel bogie
examples.lesson: Small wheel carriers and a compact upright mounting pair create aircraft landing gear with a clear silhouette.
examples.placement_notes: This System aircraft fitting contains a few Technic connector pieces. Match the upper mounting interface and tyre ground plane to the host aircraft; this is not a retracting mechanism recipe. Connection analysis leaves 5 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Faceted research-ship bow
examples.lesson: Side-stud bricks and small slopes shape a compact ship bow in multiple directions without scaling any physical part.
examples.placement_notes: The source axes do not present the bow as a complete horizontal hull. Consult the parent placement matrix before orienting it, and continue its red, dark blue and grey bands into the adjoining hull. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

examples.title: Rounded cockpit shell
examples.lesson: Repeated curved roof pieces form a smooth shell while narrow side ledges leave space for a cockpit or nose insert.
examples.placement_notes: The source shell is six studs wide and open at one end and underneath. Preserve the ledges and rear opening, then build the glazing, floor and host attachments for the new model.

examples.title: Fire-escape railing insert
examples.lesson: Bars and articulated small elements produce thin open ironwork that reads more delicately than stacked wall bricks.
examples.placement_notes: This is a railing insert and support strip from a larger fire escape, not a complete stair. Preserve the angled bar connections and locate the strip in its floor or balcony context.

examples.title: Classical arch and cornice
examples.lesson: A moulded arch, grooved masonry and round plates under the cornice create shadow lines in a shallow facade bay.
examples.placement_notes: The source is only one stud deep and has two separate pier feet. Tie both piers into the host base and continue the cornice rhythm; use the parameterized arcade recipe for another height.

examples.title: Park bench with shaped back
examples.lesson: Dedicated shaped back elements and a mostly tiled seat create a recognizable bench with a low part count.
examples.placement_notes: Reserve eight studs of width and the backrest overhang beyond the two-stud seat. Attach the two white feet to the pavement and keep the seat studs accessible if adding figures.

examples.title: Arcade Bay recipe
examples.lesson: Change height and palette using real brick courses; preserve the assembly interfaces.

examples.title: Street Lantern recipe
examples.lesson: Change height and palette using real brick courses; preserve the assembly interfaces.

examples.title: Two-axle train bogie with buffers and magnetic coupling
examples.lesson: Combine two wheelsets, a bogie pivot and a coupling on one supported undercarriage; minifigure heads become buffer faces.
examples.placement_notes: The locomotive chassis and receiving mount for the bogie pin. The parent turns this assembly 90 degrees about Y and places it at [-170, 56, 0]. It does not provide a motor or powered transmission for this bogie. Keep the wheelsets, pin and coupling stack together. Reserve turning space around the bogie and buffer faces; do not assume clearance on a different chassis or track curve.

examples.title: Balcony facade with door, dormer and planted railing
examples.lesson: Integrate a balcony floor, door threshold, decorative railing and sloped roof window into a layered facade module.
examples.placement_notes: The building below, side/rear enclosure and surrounding roof. The complete-model parent places this section at [78, -185, 120], rotated 180 degrees about Y. Its plate underside needs support across the host building. Preserve the door opening and plate support grid. Rebuild wall courses when changing width; do not stretch the roof window, fencing or glazing.

examples.title: Compact aircraft landing strut with matched wheel and tyre
examples.lesson: Use a short axle and two angle connectors to separate the fuselage mounting pin from a freely mounted wheel.
examples.placement_notes: The fuselage Technic receiving bricks and the placement angle. The parent contains two differently rotated occurrences at X = -50 and +50; the extracted strut is not already in its installed orientation. Keep the wheel/tyre pair and pin roles. Measure the host receiving hole before placement and review the complete fuselage clearance. Six optimistic connection groups remain for seven placements: this is a geometry study, not a verified mechanical core.

examples.title: Hinged spacecraft side hatch with bracket-mounted engine cone
examples.lesson: Carry an engine cone, fin and layered side shell on a hinged module while leaving the mating hinge half in the hull.
examples.placement_notes: The mating 3830 hinge top: the hull places it at [-60, -128, 240], beside the hatch occurrence at [-60, -72, 240]. The opposite hatch is a separately authored section, not permission to reflect rigid parts. Copy or rebuild the hull-side hinge support before claiming an attached hatch. Preserve hinge alignment and reserve the swept space; opening travel is not checked by this static source.

examples.title: Small warehouse forklift with dedicated lifting mast
examples.lesson: Build a complete small service vehicle around a dedicated mast rather than inventing a lifting linkage from loose parts.
examples.placement_notes: Cargo, a cart, the aircraft and minifigures are separate scene objects. No structural part of this forklift is supplied by the parent. Its inherited body colour is red (4); the isolated xray board uses its default yellow for inherited colour. Preserve the mast and matched wheel/tyre pairs. Change surrounding bodywork and palette, then check ground contact and fork clearance. Cargo fit, load stability and lift travel remain unverified.

examples.title: Seven-part swivel armchair with sideways tiled armrests
examples.lesson: Turn a moulded seat into a compact armchair using opposing brackets, sideways tiles and a complete turntable pair.
examples.placement_notes: Only the room/floor context; both turntable halves are included. The source places the chair at an angle through a proper Y rotation, rather than changing its internal construction. Keep the bracket offsets and turntable pair. Recolour or place the whole chair, leaving room around its armrests; verify floor attachment separately when mounting it.
